name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/B1
top_fix: Move the 'Proposed Exercise 4 solution' code block out of astraupskill/05-PRACTICE.md into 06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md and fix the stale 'service-regression-06' reference to service-regression-07.
summary: Real confidentiality bug in a Next.js incident-response API: getIncidentDetail authorized the selected incident but embedded parent/child incidents by ID alone, so a viewer of a public child received the whole confidential parent. Fix reuses the existing canViewIncident predicate at both relation boundaries; a 128-line Node harness asserts hidden IDs, absent secret titles, retained admin/responder/assignee exceptions, exactly 9 mocked reads and zero writes. VERIFICATION is candid, even naming an earlier mock that targeted the wrong module copy. Weaknesses are form: unbroken prose, no sub-headings, one solution leaking into the practice file, and 4000 words for a six-line diff.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/D1
top_fix: Add a vocabulary section (LexoRank, presence, outbox, optimistic version, DI seam) and explain the Parameters<Parameters<typeof db.transaction>[0]>[0] idiom; fix package.json 'seed' pointing at a nonexistent prisma/seed.ts and delete the dead next.config.ts.
summary: Four genuinely different production bugs fixed in one realtime Kanban app: board:join joined the Socket.IO room and wrote presence before authorization; card:update had no payload schema; updateCardDetails used '?? undefined' so an explicit null clear was swallowed; and appendBoardEvent read the board version outside the transaction before writing it. Four Node tests drive the real registration function via a FakeSocket and assert the exact Drizzle .set argument. Also fixes a real Next.js misuse (calling headers() from next/headers inside a socket handler). Hardest course in the batch; about half the practice exercises are reasoning-only for lack of a DB harness.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/e13

summary: Excellent subject matter, poor delivery. The refund fix is subtle and correct: the original compared cumulative SUCCEEDED refunds against a payment.amountCaptured that it was also decrementing, so a legitimate second partial refund was rejected. Idempotency keys are now bound to (paymentId, kind, amount) in both orders.ts and webhooks.ts, and duplicate fulfillment lines that could double-consume a reservation are rejected. But the course has zero code blocks in nine files, 03-WORKED-CHANGE says the order/warehouse checks run before the Prisma transaction when they run inside it, the warehouse allocation check was pre-existing but claimed as new, and the README repeats its navigation paragraph three times.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/e6
top_fix: Add a root 'test' script (tsx --test apps/api/tests/*.test.ts) so the suite is runnable and CI-callable instead of requiring a hand-copied six-token command, and document the required prior npm run build.
summary: Best-taught course in the batch. Four distinct real defects in a Fastify + Socket.IO workspace API: MemoryStore.getWorkspace had no membership check at all; the bootstrap inbox returned every member's notifications; createIssue accepted foreign project/issueType/status/assignee/label ids; and the socket disconnect handler never removed the disconnecting socket's presence while trusting a client-supplied memberId. Eight tests, including a real Fastify app.inject round trip asserting 200/403/404 through a typed StoreError. The practice chapter is the only one that tells you how to know your test is valid (structuredClone, because Object.assign mutates the object you meant to compare against).

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/w24

summary: A feature-flag platform teaching four things well: authorize at the service not only at the route, validate shape before it becomes runtime behavior, keep multi-record writes in one boundary and invalidate cache only after commit, and never echo an internal error to the client. The rollback test stubs auditService.record to throw then deep-compares the entire mock database plus the cache, and another test posts '{bad' to the real POST route handler and asserts 400 with no mutation. Marked IMPROVE despite an average of 4.0 because the centerpiece worked-change chapter shows a repository API that does not exist, and the documented reproduce command runs 9 of the 11 delivered tests (VERIFICATION cites a superseded 9-test record).

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/ww17

summary: Best Prisma transaction content in the batch buried under the worst padding. It fixes a real cross-tenant write: the old updateStatus called prisma.playbookRun.update({where:{id}}) with no tenant predicate and compared tenantId only after the commit. The replacement is a tenant-scoped findFirst plus updateMany compare-and-set on expectedStatus with the audit row in the same $transaction, a zero count surfacing as a retryable error; health-config publish commits config, snapshots and audit together with the version read moved inside the transaction and a new @@unique([tenantId, version]). But the worked-change chapter has no code at all, VERIFICATION.md is Astra's internal handoff checklist (including 'confirm nine guides meet the minimum word count'), and all 12 tests exercise the mock adapter while the limits imply a Next build validates Prisma transaction behavior.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/ww27
top_fix: Fix astraupskill/VERIFICATION.md: it cites the superseded record ww27-test-08.json and says '10 tests', while that log reads 11 and the delivery's final record ww27-test-18.json reads 12 - three numbers for one suite, with the course citing the oldest.
summary: API versioning done right at the code level. The old v1/v2 adapters typed version as a known union and used a bare if (version === 'v1') ... else return v2Shape, so any unsupported version silently got v2 semantics; the fix adds runtime assertSupportedVersion plus per-shape type guards. It also adds CLIENT ownership checks, rollout validation (integer 0-100, unique non-blank allowlist) before writes, compensation when the audit write fails, and - a nice catch - repairs three files whose header comments contained '**/route.ts', where the embedded '*/' terminated the block comment and broke the file. Teaching is thin: zero code blocks in nine files, every file has two H1 headings from two concatenated documents, and VERIFICATION is a delivery checklist.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/ww37
top_fix: Teach the Next 15 async params migration that the change silently performed (all three dynamic routes moved to params: Promise<{...}> with await params) and add a 'why validate twice' paragraph explaining the route-level zod schemas versus the new service-level asserts.
summary: Strongest all-round package. Two real bugs: PATCH /api/items passed all four metadata fields so an omitted name arrived as undefined and the repository's {...current, ...patch} spread erased the stored SKU; and createHold read-modified-wrote with no serialization so two service instances could each approve seven units out of ten. Fixed with a key-by-key patch builder (!== undefined, so reorderPoint 0 survives) and a repository-owned promise-tail mutex that snapshots and restores all three Maps on throw. Thirteen tests including one written purely to document a limitation (an unlocked read can observe a suspended callback), and the most reproducible VERIFICATION in the batch: pinned Node 22.16.0, npm ci, PowerShell with exit-code guards after every command.
